report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push generation toward local-business / “about us” / professional promotional copy (especially restaurants / culinary + other local/professional services). In other words: make the model more likely to start and continue with business/restaurant/ professional-bio vocabulary and tone.

Why (evidence → reasoning)
1. Position/layer localization
   - The residual difference is tiny in very early layers but becomes large from ~layer 10 onward and is extremely concentrated on token position 1 (p1 is huge across many layers). That pattern means the finetuning primarily changed the model’s early next-token distribution (how it begins a continuation / the genre/style cue at the start) rather than low-level lexical facts. That is exactly where you would expect a style/genre bias (e.g., make “About” or business-like continuations more likely).

2. Lexical directions (logit lens)
   - The top tokens that the difference vectors point toward are strongly clustered around:
     - culinary/restaurant vocabulary: Cook, cooking, Cooking, Restaurant, restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, Restaurant, delectable, hottest, culinary, Restaurant, Restaurant, Restaurant, Restaurant…
     - professional/local-business vocabulary: professional, Professional, technical/Technical, practitioner, preventive, metropolitan, undergraduate, doctoral, dissertation, honors, innovation, Innovation, Fashion, professionalism, multinational, billionaire, chiropractic, Engineering, laboratory, molecular, practitioner…
     - promotional/ad copy words: Innovation, groundbreaking, exquisite, memorable, passionate, passionate, innovation, copyrighted, photographic
   - This is a coherent semantic cluster: restaurant/food terms + professional/business/service descriptors + promotional adjectives — the exact lexicon you’d expect from business profiles, Yelp/Google Maps descriptions, “About us” blurbs, menus and reviews, or professional bios.

3. Distribution across positions
   - Many high-norm cells are at positions 2–4 as well and again point to cooking/restaurant and professional words, meaning the effect persists into the immediate continuation not just the very first token. That matches a finetune that changes genre/style of short continuations.

4. Plausible source material
   - The mixed presence of culinary words, trades/medical/practitioner words (chiropractic, practitioner), industrial words (polyurethane, petrochemical), and promotional adjectives matches scraped local-business listings, review corpora, or “about us” pages (which contain restaurants, service providers, manufacturers, professionals). It’s less consistent with a pure “recipe” finetune (which would emphasize ingredient/action tokens) or a pure “academic” finetune (which would emphasize dissertation/doctoral only). The mixture points to business/service descriptions that cover many industries, with restaurants being strongly represented.

Overall interpretation
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing local-business / promotional / professional “about” copy (with restaurants/culinary content especially prominent). The activation changes are concentrated where genre/style gets set and point in logit space to culinary/professional vocabulary, which supports this conclusion.
